speaker: Doctor
text: The infant is well-appearing with no systemic symptoms or mucosal involvement, and the rash spares the palms and soles, which strongly points away from infectious causes like congenital syphilis. Given the presence of pustules on an erythematous base appearing around day 3-4 of life in a term infant, this is classic for transient neonatal pustular melanosis or erythema toxicum neonatorum. I will request a Gram stain and culture of the pustules to definitively rule out bacterial infection before finalizing the diagnosis. REQUEST TEST: Gram_stain_and_culture_of_pustules

speaker: Doctor
text: The Gram stain and culture results are negative, which effectively rules out a bacterial infection like staphylococcal scalded skin syndrome or impetigo. Given the infant is well-appearing, the rash appeared at day 3, and it consists of erythematous maculopapules and pustules sparing the palms and soles, the clinical picture is classic for erythema toxicum neonatorum. DIAGNOSIS READY: Erythema toxicum neonatorum
